app.name: Vitals
app.tagline: See what your computer is actually doing.

confirm.endBody: Unsaved work in this app will be lost.
confirm.endCriticalBody: Ending it will make Windows unstable and may cause a restart or data loss.
confirm.safe: Unsaved work in this app will be lost.
confirm.disruptive: This will close your desktop and any open windows. It usually restarts on its own.
confirm.critical: The system depends on this. Ending it will crash Windows immediately and you will lose unsaved work in every app.
confirm.forbidden: Windows protects this process. It cannot be ended, even as an administrator.
confirm.denied: Windows refused: this process belongs to another account or to the system. Retrying as administrator asks for approval once, for this action only.

empty.title: No process matches
empty.body: Clear the search or choose a different filter.

noSampler.title: No readings are arriving
noSampler.body: Vitals cannot reach the part of itself that measures your computer. Nothing is wrong with the computer — restarting Vitals usually fixes this.

detail.title: Details
detail.none: Select a process to see its details.

capability.noSuchHardware: Your hardware does not report this
capability.appSandbox: Not allowed in the App Store version. The download from the website can do this.

kind.accessDenied: Windows would not allow that. Running Vitals as an administrator usually fixes it.
kind.notFound: That is no longer there — it may have been removed or renamed.
kind.unsupported: This copy of Vitals cannot do that on this computer.

sampling.title: Sampling
sampling.backgroundThrottleHint: Keeps Vitals near-zero cost when you are not looking at it.

history.title: History
history.enableHint: Stored only on this computer. Off by default.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.noTelemetry: Vitals collects nothing about you and sends it nowhere.
privacy.localOnly: Everything it measures stays on this computer. History, if you turn it on, is a local file you can delete.
privacy.noCrashReports: There is no crash reporting and no usage analytics. If Vitals crashes, it writes crash.txt in its own folder for you to attach to a bug report — it never sends it.
privacy.noLookups: No file is ever hashed or looked up online.
privacy.lanServer: The LAN server for your phone and other tools is off until you turn it on, and only answers devices on your own network. A local-only connection on 127.0.0.1 is always open so the vitals command-line tool can reach the app.
privacy.updates: The only request Vitals makes by itself is an update check to GitHub, about 20 seconds after launch. GitHub sees your IP address and the app version, as with any download. Turn it off under About.
privacy.updatesStore: Vitals makes no requests by itself. Updates come from the Microsoft Store.
privacy.updatesMacAppStore: Vitals makes no requests by itself. Updates come from the Mac App Store.

about.title: About
about.contribute: Vitals is free and open source, forever.
about.contributeBody: Found a bug or want a feature? Open an issue on GitHub — every report makes it better.

update.title: Updates
update.idle: Vitals can check GitHub for a newer version.
update.upToDate: You are running the latest version.
update.unconfigured: Updates are not configured for this build.
update.unconfiguredHint: Development and unsigned builds cannot verify an update. Download the latest release from GitHub instead.
update.autoHint: Checks GitHub shortly after launch and installs a signed update when you quit, or once you have been away for ten minutes with Vitals only in the tray. Nothing is installed while you are using Vitals.
update.store: Updates come from the Microsoft Store.
update.macAppStore: Updates come from the Mac App Store.
update.pending: Version {{version}} is downloaded. It installs when you quit Vitals, or the next time you step away for ten minutes.
update.pendingApproval: Version {{version}} is downloaded. Vitals is installed for everyone on this PC, so Windows asks an administrator to approve the update. Restart to update when you are ready.
update.failedToastHint: Vitals will try again. You can also restart to update from Settings › About.
update.leftover: An older copy of Vitals is still installed for everyone in {{path}}. This copy now updates without asking for administrator rights; the old one can go.
update.leftoverFailed: The old copy could not be removed
update.moveHint: Vitals is installed for everyone on this PC, so every update asks an administrator to approve it. Moving it to your own account stops that, and the old copy can be removed afterwards.
update.moveLosesTaskManager: Moving Vitals to your account turns off “Replace Task Manager” in Settings › General: the replacement only works from a copy in Program Files, where Windows can vouch for it, and a per-account copy cannot live there. Ctrl+Shift+Esc will open Windows Task Manager again.

suppressed.packaged: The Microsoft Store keeps this copy up to date.
suppressed.development: Development build: the background updater stays off.
suppressed.environment: Disabled by the VITALS_NO_AUTO_UPDATE environment variable.

hud.title: Vitals
hud.clickThroughHint: Clicks pass through to whatever is behind. Press Ctrl+Shift+H to bring it back.

mobile.pairExpiredBody: This computer no longer accepts the phone's key. Open Vitals on the PC and scan a fresh code.

empty.title: No PC is paired yet
empty.body: On the computer you want to watch, open Vitals → Settings → Remote access, turn it on, then scan the QR code it shows with this phone's camera.
empty.pairFailedBody: The computer did not answer, or the code has expired. Show a fresh QR code on the PC and scan it again.

processes.title: Processes
processes.noneBody: No process on this computer matches what you typed.
processes.pickMachineBody: Open the Machines tab and tap the computer whose processes you want to see.

action.title: What should {{name}} do?
action.confirmHint: Tap again to confirm. Unsaved work in this app will be lost.
action.readOnlyBody: Re-pair it from the PC with control allowed if you want to end tasks from here.
action.denied: Windows would not let Vitals touch this process

settings.title: Settings
settings.themeFollows: Follows your phone's light or dark setting.
settings.pairAnotherBody: Open Vitals on that computer, go to Settings → Remote access, and scan its QR code with this phone.

projects.title: Codwen projects
projects.stale: Showing the last list; the latest refresh failed.
projects.readOnly: Read-only: Vitals lists your projects and their health from your Codwen account. It never changes a project, and never probes one itself.

empty.title: No projects yet
empty.body: Your Codwen account has no projects yet. Create one on codwen.com and it will appear here.

unavailable.title: Projects are not available yet
unavailable.body: Vitals can read your Codwen projects, but the endpoint that reports their health has not been released yet. This tab will fill in on its own once it is.

error.title: Could not reach Codwen
error.body: Vitals could not read your projects. Check your connection and try again.

noHost.title: No data arriving
noHost.body: Vitals cannot reach the component that reads your Codwen account. Restarting Vitals usually fixes this.

devcloud.title: Devcloud workspaces
devcloud.runs_one: {{count}} cloud run in the last {{hours}} h
devcloud.runs_other: {{count}} cloud runs in the last {{hours}} h
devcloud.healthy: No cloud workspace is marked down.
devcloud.down: {{ws}} is unavailable until {{until}} — runs go local.
devcloud.noHost: Vitals cannot reach the component that runs agentq here.
devcloud.unreachable: The live status could not be read. Showing the last reading.
devcloud.dashNote: An em dash is a value agentq did not measure — it is never a zero.
devcloud.failureNoAgentq: agentq is not installed here, so there is no live status to read.
devcloud.failureBlocked: The live status was not read, for a safety reason.
devcloud.failureFailed: The agentq status command did not finish.
devcloud.failureUnparsable: agentq answered with something Vitals could not read.
